playbook:
- Retained gold scores 2 points per unit; deposited gold scores 1 point per unit. Depositing anything at all is strictly worse than keeping it. When the deposit stage is put to me, I deposit 0, every round, no exceptions.

- Do not talk myself into "depositing to stay consistent with my declaration" or "to maximize committed value." Consistency earns nothing; only gold earns points. That reasoning cost me every match against an opponent who deposited 0.

- Declarations are not scored. There is no prize for the highest declared figure, so do not over-declare to "outbid" anyone — that reasoning was wrong and gained nothing.

- Since deposits are capped by my declaration and I plan to deposit 0 anyway, the declaration only creates audit risk. When the declare stage is put to me, I declare my true yield — never higher. Over-declaring exposes me to the inspection dock with zero upside.

- When an opponent announces aggressive inspections, that is extra confirmation to declare truthfully, not a reason to change anything else.

- Ignore the opponent's score gap as a reason to take risks. Being behind does not make depositing or over-declaring better; the best response to an opponent who free-rides is to also retain everything, which out-scores them per unit of yield.

- Never under-declare either: a low declaration gains nothing since I deposit 0 regardless, and truthful declarations keep me safe from any audit.

- Simple rule for every round: declare my true yield, deposit 0, retain everything. Each round that yields me 2× my yield in points, which beats any line that sends gold to the treasury.
